sanskrit: tam ekaṃ bahubhir dṛṣṭvā pīḍyamānaṃ mahārathaiḥ sādhuvādo mahāñ jajñe siddhāś cāsan praharṣitāḥ āścaryam ity abhāṣanta munayaś cāpi saṃgatāḥ
english: Seeing him, one man, beset by many great chariot-warriors, a vast cry of approval arose, and the Siddhas were thrilled; the sages too, gathered there, exclaimed, "A wonder!"

sanskrit: bhīmaseno raṇe śalyaṃ śalyabhūtaṃ parākrame ekena viddhvā bāṇena punar vivyādha saptabhiḥ
english: In the battle Bhīmasena, having pierced Śalya—who was like a barb in his valor—with a single arrow, struck him again with seven.

sanskrit: sātyakiś ca śatenainaṃ dharmaputraparīpsayā madreśvaram avākīrya siṃhanādam athānadat
english: And Sātyaki, longing to protect the son of Dharma, overwhelmed the lord of the Madras with a hundred shafts and then let loose a lion's roar.

sanskrit: nakulaḥ pañcabhiś cainaṃ sahadevaś ca saptabhiḥ viddhvā taṃ tu tatas tūrṇaṃ punar vivyādha saptabhiḥ
english: Nakula pierced him with five and Sahadeva with seven, and then swiftly struck him once more with seven.

sanskrit: sa tu śūro raṇe yattaḥ pīḍitas tair mahārathaiḥ vikṛṣya kārmukaṃ ghoraṃ vegaghnaṃ bhārasādhanam
english: But that hero, intent in the fray and hard-pressed by those great chariot-warriors, drew his dreadful bow—deadly in its speed, equal to its heavy task.

sanskrit: sātyakiṃ pañcaviṃśatyā śalyo vivyādha māriṣa bhīmasenaṃ trisaptatyā nakulaṃ saptabhis tathā
english: Śalya pierced Sātyaki with twenty-five arrows, O lord, Bhīmasena with seventy-three, and Nakula with seven.

sanskrit: tataḥ saviśikhaṃ cāpaṃ sahadevasya dhanvinaḥ chittvā bhallena samare vivyādhainaṃ trisaptabhiḥ
english: Then, cutting the bow of the archer Sahadeva together with its nocked arrow by a broad-headed shaft in the battle, he pierced him with twenty-one.

sanskrit: sahadevas tu samare mātulaṃ bhūrivarcasam sajyam anyad dhanuḥ kṛtvā pañcabhiḥ samatāḍayat śarair āśīviṣākārair jvalaj jvalanasaṃnibhaiḥ
english: But Sahadeva in the fray, stringing another bow, struck his uncle of abundant splendor with five arrows shaped like venomous serpents, blazing like flaming fire.

sanskrit: sārathiṃ cāsya samare śareṇānataparvaṇā vivyādha bhṛśasaṃkruddhas taṃ ca bhūyas tribhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: And in the battle, exceedingly enraged, he pierced his charioteer with a smooth-jointed arrow, and the man again with three more shafts.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas trisaptatyā sātyakir navabhiḥ śaraiḥ dharmarājas tathā ṣaṣṭyā gātre śalyaṃ samarpayat
english: Bhīmasena with seventy-three, Sātyaki with nine arrows, and the king of righteousness with sixty planted their shafts in Śalya's body.

sanskrit: tataḥ śalyo mahārāja nirviddhas tair mahārathaiḥ susrāva rudhiraṃ gātrair gairikaṃ parvato yathā
english: Then, O great king, Śalya, pierced through by those great chariot-warriors, streamed blood from his limbs as a mountain streams red ochre.

sanskrit: tāṃś ca sarvān maheṣvāsān pañcabhiḥ pañcabhiḥ śaraiḥ vivyādha tarasā rājaṃs tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: And he pierced all those mighty archers, five arrows to each, with such force, O king, that it seemed a marvel.

sanskrit: tato 'pareṇa bhallena dharmaputrasya māriṣa dhanuś ciccheda samare sajyaṃ sa sumahārathaḥ
english: Then with another broad-headed shaft, O lord, that mighty chariot-warrior cut apart the strung bow of the son of Dharma in the battle.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya dharmaputro mahārathaḥ sāśvasūtadhvajarathaṃ śalyaṃ prācchādayac charaiḥ
english: Then, taking up another bow, the son of Dharma, that great chariot-warrior, covered Śalya over with arrows—horses, charioteer, banner, and car alike.

sanskrit: sa cchādyamānaḥ samare dharmaputrasya sāyakaiḥ yudhiṣṭhiram athāvidhyad daśabhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Being so covered in the fray by the shafts of Dharma's son, he in turn pierced Yudhiṣṭhira with ten sharp arrows.

sanskrit: sātyakis tu tataḥ kruddho dharmaputre śarārdite madrāṇām adhipaṃ śūraṃ śaraughaiḥ samavārayat
english: Then Sātyaki, enraged when the son of Dharma was sore wounded by arrows, held off the valiant lord of the Madras with floods of shafts.

sanskrit: sa sātyakeḥ praciccheda kṣurapreṇa mahad dhanuḥ bhīmasenamukhāṃs tāṃś ca tribhis tribhir atāḍayat
english: He cut apart Sātyaki's great bow with a razor-tipped shaft, and struck those warriors led by Bhīmasena, three arrows to each.

sanskrit: tasya kruddho mahārāja sātyakiḥ satyavikramaḥ tomaraṃ preṣayām āsa svarṇadaṇḍaṃ mahādhanam
english: Enraged at him, O great king, Sātyaki of true valor hurled a lance, gold-shafted and of great worth.

sanskrit: bhīmaseno 'tha nārācaṃ jvalantam iva pannagam nakulaḥ samare śaktiṃ sahadevo gadāṃ śubhām dharmarājaḥ śataghnīṃ tu jighāṃsuḥ śalyam āhave
english: Bhīmasena then an iron shaft blazing like a serpent, Nakula a spear in the fray, Sahadeva a fair mace, and the king of righteousness a hundred-slayer—each bent on slaying Śalya in the battle.

sanskrit: tān āpatata evāśu pañcānāṃ vai bhujacyutān sātyakiprahitaṃ śalyo bhallaiś ciccheda tomaram
english: As these missiles, loosed from the arms of the five, came hurtling swiftly down, Śalya cut the lance flung by Sātyaki to pieces with his broad-headed shafts.

sanskrit: bhīmena prahitaṃ cāpi śaraṃ kanakabhūṣaṇam dvidhā ciccheda samare kṛtahastaḥ pratāpavān
english: And the gold-adorned arrow sped by Bhīma, that deft-handed and glorious warrior cut in two within the battle.

sanskrit: nakulapreṣitāṃ śaktiṃ hemadaṇḍāṃ bhayāvahām gadāṃ ca sahadevena śaraughaiḥ samavārayat
english: The dreadful, gold-shafted spear sent by Nakula, and the mace by Sahadeva, he warded off with floods of arrows.

sanskrit: śarābhyāṃ ca śataghnīṃ tāṃ rājñaś ciccheda bhārata paśyatāṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ siṃhanādaṃ nanāda ca nāmṛṣyat taṃ tu śaineyaḥ śatror vijayam āhave
english: And with two arrows he cut apart that hundred-slayer of the king, O Bhārata, before the eyes of Pāṇḍu's sons, and roared a lion's roar; but the grandson of Śini could not endure the foe's triumph in the battle.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya sātyakiḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ dvābhyāṃ madreśvaraṃ viddhvā sārathiṃ ca tribhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then, seizing another bow, Sātyaki, swooning with rage, pierced the lord of the Madras with two arrows and his charioteer with three.

sanskrit: tataḥ śalyo mahārāja sarvāṃs tān daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ vivyādha subhṛśaṃ kruddhas tottrair iva mahādvipān
english: Then Śalya, O great king, exceedingly wrathful, pierced them all with ten arrows each, as one goads great elephants with prods.

sanskrit: te vāryamāṇāḥ samare madrarājñā mahārathāḥ na śekuḥ pramukhe sthātuṃ tasya śatruniṣūdanāḥ
english: Held back in the fray by the king of the Madras, those great chariot-warriors, slayers of foes though they were, could not stand before his face.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā dṛṣṭvā śalyasya vikramam nihatān pāṇḍavān mene pāñcālān atha sṛñjayān
english: Then King Duryodhana, beholding Śalya's prowess, deemed the Pāṇḍavas, the Pāñcālas, and the Sṛñjayas already slain.

sanskrit: tato rājan mahābāhur bhīmasenaḥ pratāpavān saṃtyajya manasā prāṇān madrādhipam ayodhayat
english: Then, O king, the mighty-armed and glorious Bhīmasena, resigning his very life in his heart, gave battle to the lord of the Madras.

sanskrit: nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca sātyakiś ca mahārathaḥ parivārya tadā śalyaṃ samantād vyakirañ śaraiḥ
english: Nakula and Sahadeva, and Sātyaki the great chariot-warrior, surrounding Śalya then, covered him on every side with arrows.

sanskrit: sa caturbhir maheṣvāsaiḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathaiḥ vṛtas tān yodhayām āsa madrarājaḥ pratāpavān
english: Encircled by those four mighty archers, the great chariot-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas, the glorious king of the Madras gave them battle.

sanskrit: tasya dharmasuto rājan kṣurapreṇa mahāhave cakrarakṣaṃ jaghānāśu madrarājasya pārthiva
english: In that great battle, O king, the son of Dharma with a razor-tipped shaft swiftly slew the wheel-guard of the king of the Madras, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu nihate śūre cakrarakṣe mahārathe madrarājo 'tibalavān sainikān āstṛṇoc charaiḥ
english: But when that valiant wheel-guard, a great chariot-warrior, was slain, the exceedingly mighty king of the Madras strewed down the soldiers with his arrows.

sanskrit: samācchannāṃs tatas tāṃs tu rājan vīkṣya sa sainikān cintayām āsa samare dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Then, O king, beholding those soldiers overwhelmed in the fray, the king of righteousness, Yudhiṣṭhira, fell to pondering.

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu na bhavet satyaṃ tan mādhavavaco mahat na hi kruddho raṇe rājā kṣapayeta balaṃ mama
english: "How shall that great word of Mādhava not prove true? Surely this king, enraged in battle, will not consume my host!"

sanskrit: tataḥ sarathanāgāśvāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ pāṇḍupūrvaja madreśvaraṃ samāseduḥ pīḍayantaḥ samantataḥ
english: Then, O elder-born of Pāṇḍu's line, the Pāṇḍavas with their chariots, elephants, and horses closed upon the lord of the Madras, beleaguering him on every side.

sanskrit: nānāśastraughabahulāṃ śastravṛṣṭiṃ samutthitām vyadhamat samare rājan mahābhrāṇīva mārutaḥ
english: The rain of weapons, swollen with floods of manifold arms, that rose against him, he scattered in the fray, O king, as the wind scatters great clouds.

sanskrit: tataḥ kanakapuṅkhāṃ tāṃ śalyakṣiptāṃ viyadgatām śaravṛṣṭim apaśyāma śalabhānām ivātatim
english: Then we beheld that rain of gold-feathered arrows, loosed by Śalya and gone aloft into the sky, like an extending swarm of locusts.

sanskrit: te śarā madrarājena preṣitā raṇamūrdhani saṃpatantaḥ sma dṛśyante śalabhānāṃ vrajā iva
english: Those arrows sped by the king of the Madras at the battle's front were seen falling together like flocks of locusts.

sanskrit: madrarājadhanurmuktaiḥ śaraiḥ kanakabhūṣaṇaiḥ nirantaram ivākāśaṃ saṃbabhūva janādhipa
english: By the gold-adorned arrows loosed from the bow of the king of the Madras, the very sky became, as it were, without a gap, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: na pāṇḍavānāṃ nāsmākaṃ tatra kaś cid vyadṛśyata bāṇāndhakāre mahati kṛte tatra mahābhaye
english: Neither of the Pāṇḍavas nor of our own host could anyone there be seen, so great and dreadful was the darkness of arrows wrought in that place of terror.

sanskrit: madrarājena balinā lāghavāc charavṛṣṭibhiḥ loḍyamānaṃ tathā dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavānāṃ balārṇavam vismayaṃ paramaṃ jagmur devagandharvadānavāḥ
english: Beholding the ocean-like host of the Pāṇḍavas churned thus by the mighty king of the Madras with his swift rains of arrows, the gods, gandharvas, and dānavas fell into the utmost wonder.

sanskrit: sa tu tān sarvato yattāñ śaraiḥ saṃpīḍya māriṣa dharmarājam avacchādya siṃhavad vyanadan muhuḥ
english: But he, beleaguering with arrows those who pressed from every side, O lord, and covering over the king of righteousness, roared again and again like a lion.

sanskrit: te channāḥ samare tena pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathāḥ na śekus taṃ tadā yuddhe pratyudyātuṃ mahāratham
english: Covered over by him in the fray, those great chariot-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas could not then come forth against that great car-warrior in the battle.

sanskrit: dharmarājapurogās tu bhīmasenamukhā rathāḥ na jahuḥ samare śūraṃ śalyam āhavaśobhinam
english: Yet those car-warriors, led by the king of righteousness and headed by Bhīmasena, did not forsake the fray against the valiant Śalya, the splendor of the battle.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca arjuno drauṇinā viddho yuddhe bahubhir āyasaiḥ tasya cānucaraiḥ śūrais trigartānāṃ mahārathaiḥ drauṇiṃ vivyādha samare tribhir eva śilīmukhaiḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Arjuna, pierced in the fight by Droṇa's son with many iron shafts, and by his valiant followers, the great chariot-warriors of the Trigartas, pierced Droṇa's son in the battle with but three sharp-pointed arrows.

sanskrit: tathetarān maheṣvāsān dvābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ bhūyaś caiva mahābāhuḥ śaravarṣair avākirat
english: And the other mighty archers Dhanaṃjaya pierced, two arrows to each, and the mighty-armed one moreover overwhelmed them with showers of shafts.

sanskrit: śarakaṇṭakitās te tu tāvakā bharatarṣabha na jahuḥ samare pārthaṃ vadhyamānāḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: But your men, O bull of the Bharatas, bristling with arrows like thorns, did not forsake Pārtha in the fray, though slain by his keen shafts.

sanskrit: te 'rjunaṃ rathavaṃśena droṇaputrapurogamāḥ ayodhayanta samare parivārya mahārathāḥ
english: With a line of chariots, led by the son of Droṇa, those great car-warriors surrounded Arjuna and gave him battle in the fray.

sanskrit: tais tu kṣiptāḥ śarā rājan kārtasvaravibhūṣitāḥ arjunasya rathopasthaṃ pūrayām āsur añjasā
english: The arrows hurled by them, O king, adorned with gold, straightway filled the floor of Arjuna's chariot.

sanskrit: tathā kṛṣṇau maheṣvāsau vṛṣabhau sarvadhanvinām śarair vīkṣya vitunnāṅgau prahṛṣṭau yuddhadurmadau
english: And the two Kṛṣṇas, those mighty archers, bulls among all bowmen, beholding their limbs pierced through with arrows, grew exultant, irresistible in battle.

sanskrit: kūbaraṃ rathacakrāṇi īṣā yoktrāṇi cābhibho yugaṃ caivānukarṣaṃ ca śarabhūtam abhūt tadā
english: The pole, the chariot-wheels, the shaft, the harness-cords, O lord, the yoke and the under-pole—all then became, as it were, made of arrows.

sanskrit: naitādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ rājan naiva ca naḥ śrutam yādṛśaṃ tatra pārthasya tāvakāḥ saṃpracakrire
english: Never before, O king, had we seen or heard such a feat as your men there wrought upon Pārtha.

sanskrit: sa rathaḥ sarvato bhāti citrapuṅkhaiḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ ulkāśataiḥ saṃpradīptaṃ vimānam iva bhūtale
english: That chariot shone on every side with keen, bright-feathered arrows, like a celestial car ablaze upon the earth with a hundred meteors.

sanskrit: tato 'rjuno mahārāja śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ avākirat tāṃ pṛtanāṃ megho vṛṣṭyā yathācalam
english: Then Arjuna, O great king, overwhelmed that host with smooth-jointed arrows, as a cloud overwhelms a mountain with rain.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ samare pārthanāmāṅkitaiḥ śaraiḥ pārthabhūtam amanyanta prekṣamāṇās tathāvidham
english: Slain in the fray by arrows marked with Pārtha's name, they, seeing him on every side, deemed all the world become Pārtha.

sanskrit: tato 'dbhutaśarajvālo dhanuḥśabdānilo mahān senendhanaṃ dadāhāśu tāvakaṃ pārthapāvakaḥ
english: Then the fire that was Pārtha, with a wondrous flame of arrows and a great wind that was the twang of his bow, swiftly burned up your army as its fuel.

sanskrit: cakrāṇāṃ patatāṃ caiva yugānāṃ ca dharātale tūṇīrāṇāṃ patākānāṃ dhvajānāṃ ca rathaiḥ saha
english: Of wheels and yokes falling to the earth, of quivers, pennons, and banners together with the chariots,

sanskrit: īṣāṇām anukarṣāṇāṃ triveṇūnāṃ ca bhārata akṣāṇām atha yoktrāṇāṃ pratodānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: of shafts and under-poles and triple bamboo frames, O Bhārata, and of axles, harness-cords, and goads on every side,

sanskrit: śirasāṃ patatāṃ caiva kuṇḍaloṣṇīṣadhāriṇām bhujānāṃ ca mahārāja skandhānāṃ ca samantataḥ
english: and of falling heads still wearing their earrings and turbans, and of arms and shoulders, O great king, on every side—

sanskrit: chatrāṇāṃ vyajanaiḥ sārdhaṃ mukuṭānāṃ ca rāśayaḥ samadṛśyanta pārthasya rathamārgeṣu bhārata
english: heaps of parasols together with fans, and of crowns, were seen along the path of Pārtha's chariot, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: agamyarūpā pṛthivī māṃsaśoṇitakardamā babhūva bharataśreṣṭha rudrasyākrīḍanaṃ yathā bhīrūṇāṃ trāsajananī śūrāṇāṃ harṣavardhanī
english: The earth became impassable, a mire of flesh and blood, O best of the Bharatas, like the playground of Rudra—begetting terror in the timid, swelling the joy of the brave.

sanskrit: hatvā tu samare pārthaḥ sahasre dve paraṃtapa rathānāṃ savarūthānāṃ vidhūmo 'gnir iva jvalan
english: Having slain in the fray, O scorcher of foes, two thousand car-warriors together with their chariot-guards, Pārtha blazed like a smokeless fire.

sanskrit: yathā hi bhagavān agnir jagad dagdhvā carācaram vidhūmo dṛśyate rājaṃs tathā pārtho mahārathaḥ
english: For as the blessed Fire, having burned up the world of things moving and unmoving, is seen smokeless, O king, so was Pārtha, that great chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: drauṇis tu samare dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavasya parākramam rathenātipatākena pāṇḍavaṃ pratyavārayat
english: But the son of Droṇa, beholding the Pāṇḍava's prowess in the fray, withstood the Pāṇḍava with his chariot of towering banners.

sanskrit: tāv ubhau puruṣavyāghrau śvetāśvau dhanvināṃ varau samīyatus tadā tūrṇaṃ parasparavadhaiṣiṇau
english: Those two tigers among men, both with white horses, foremost of bowmen, then closed swiftly together, each seeking the other's death.

sanskrit: tayor āsīn mahārāja bāṇavarṣaṃ sudāruṇam jīmūtānāṃ yathā vṛṣṭis tapānte bharatarṣabha
english: Between them, O great king, there fell a most dreadful rain of arrows, like the downpour of rain-clouds at the close of the hot season, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: anyonyaspardhinau tau tu śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ tatakṣatur mṛdhe 'nyonyaṃ śṛṅgābhyāṃ vṛṣabhāv iva
english: Contending each with the other, the two gashed one another in the fray with smooth-jointed arrows, as two bulls gore each other with their horns.

sanskrit: tayor yuddhaṃ mahārāja ciraṃ samam ivābhavat astrāṇāṃ saṃgamaś caiva ghoras tatrābhavan mahān
english: Their battle, O great king, for a long while was as if evenly matched, and there was a clash of weapons there, dreadful and great.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunaṃ dvādaśabhī rukmapuṅkhaiḥ sutejanaiḥ vāsudevaṃ ca daśabhir drauṇir vivyādha bhārata
english: Then the son of Droṇa pierced Arjuna with twelve well-sharpened, gold-feathered shafts, and Vāsudeva with ten, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahasya bībhatsur vyākṣipad gāṇḍivaṃ dhanuḥ mānayitvā muhūrtaṃ ca guruputraṃ mahāhave
english: Then Bībhatsu, laughing, drew his Gāṇḍīva bow, having for a moment honored the teacher's son in that great battle.

sanskrit: vyaśvasūtarathaṃ cakre savyasācī mahārathaḥ mṛdupūrvaṃ tataś cainaṃ tribhir vivyādha sāyakaiḥ
english: Savyasācin, the great car-warrior, made him bereft of horses, charioteer, and chariot, and then, after first sparing him, pierced him with three arrows.

sanskrit: hatāśve tu rathe tiṣṭhan droṇaputras tv ayasmayam musalaṃ pāṇḍuputrāya cikṣepa parighopamam
english: Standing in his chariot whose horses were slain, the son of Droṇa hurled at Pāṇḍu's son an iron pestle, like an iron bludgeon.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ sahasā hemapaṭṭavibhūṣitam ciccheda saptadhā vīraḥ pārthaḥ śatrunibarhaṇaḥ
english: As it came hurtling suddenly down, adorned with bands of gold, the hero Pārtha, crusher of foes, cut it into seven pieces.

sanskrit: sa cchinnaṃ musalaṃ dṛṣṭvā drauṇiḥ paramakopanaḥ ādade parighaṃ ghoraṃ nagendraśikharopamam cikṣepa caiva pārthāya drauṇir yuddhaviśāradaḥ
english: Seeing the pestle cut apart, the son of Droṇa, in extreme wrath, took up a dreadful iron bludgeon like the peak of a lordly mountain; and Droṇa's son, skilled in war, hurled it at Pārtha.

sanskrit: tam antakam iva kruddhaṃ parighaṃ prekṣya pāṇḍavaḥ arjunas tvarito jaghne pañcabhiḥ sāyakottamaiḥ
english: Beholding that bludgeon, wrathful as Death itself, the Pāṇḍava Arjuna swiftly struck it down with five excellent arrows.

sanskrit: sa cchinnaḥ patito bhūmau pārthabāṇair mahāhave dārayan pṛthivīndrāṇāṃ manaḥ śabdena bhārata
english: Severed by Pārtha's arrows, it fell to the earth in that great battle, rending the hearts of the kings of the earth with its crash, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tato 'parais tribhir bāṇair drauṇiṃ vivyādha pāṇḍavaḥ so 'tividdho balavatā pārthena sumahābalaḥ na saṃbhrāntas tadā drauṇiḥ pauruṣe sve vyavasthitaḥ
english: Then the Pāṇḍava pierced the son of Droṇa with three more arrows; yet, though sore wounded by the mighty Pārtha, the exceedingly powerful son of Droṇa was not dismayed, but stood firm in his own manliness.

sanskrit: sudharmā tu tato rājan bhāradvājaṃ mahāratham avākirac charavrātaiḥ sarvakṣatrasya paśyataḥ
english: Then Sudharman, O king, overwhelmed the great chariot-warrior, son of Bharadvāja, with clusters of arrows, before the eyes of all the warriors.

sanskrit: tatas tu suratho 'py ājau pāñcālānāṃ mahārathaḥ rathena meghaghoṣeṇa drauṇim evābhyadhāvata
english: Then Suratha too, a great chariot-warrior of the Pāñcālas, charged in the fight upon the son of Droṇa with his thunder-roaring chariot.

sanskrit: vikarṣan vai dhanuḥ śreṣṭhaṃ sarvabhārasahaṃ dṛḍham jvalanāśīviṣanibhaiḥ śaraiś cainam avākirat
english: Drawing his finest bow, firm and able to bear every strain, he overwhelmed him with arrows like blazing venomous serpents.
